assessments.closureRisk: Low — mechanisms already survived selected physical attacks; main risk is a late gate failure reopening selection.
assessments.dominantCost: Final gate execution and source commit; low cost, near-term closure.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Run final portable and physical gates; commit exact P5 source if gates pass; graduate via structured self-release.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Local finalization: mechanism selection is complete; remaining gates are acceptance checks on an already-chosen path.

assessments.closureRisk: Medium — robustness claims are not yet earned and one budget unit may only partially separate priors from overfit.
assessments.dominantCost: Designing materially different variants and re-running probes; open-ended experimental cost.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Create 2–3 materially different Scenario/Genesis encounter variants and re-run causal-episode probes across them.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Distributed robustness surface: current fixed Genesis hides generalization; variants are needed to separate surviving priors from overfit.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Open-ended experiment with lower closability in a single budget unit than R-P5's near-complete finalization.

assessments.closureRisk: Medium — may resolve to a no-op if the narrower surface is not justified by measurable cost.
assessments.dominantCost: Dependency-graph audit and packaging candidate build; moderate.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Audit Host import/dependency graph; build smallest packaging candidate only if measurable; dogfood against World and another non-MCP consumer.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Local packaging defect: semantic compatibility already passed; the unresolved issue is import-graph cost and surface justification.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Possible no-op outcome; lower expected frontier delta than R-P5's concrete graduation.

assessments.closureRisk: High — externally blocked; cannot close until DNS recovery occurs.
assessments.dominantCost: Live experiment execution; currently blocked by external DNS dependency.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Retry no-tool incremental after DNS recovery; run no-tool replay/batch and resolved-provider controls.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Externally blocked local experiment: control-path repair is causally admitted but live experiments wait on DeepSeek DNS recovery.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Externally blocked; defer per admission principle until DNS recovery unblocks live experiments.

assessments.closureRisk: High — required authority/resource does not exist; cannot close regardless of budget.
assessments.dominantCost: External infrastructure acquisition (independent Linux/systemd host); not addressable by research budget alone.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Obtain independent Linux/systemd host; verify immutable deployment kit; provision purpose-separated signers and executor-only Trade credential.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Negative control: dominant blocker is absence of an independently administered Linux/systemd host; WSL/Windows cannot satisfy high-assurance separation.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Required authority/resource does not exist; DEFER per admission principle. Negative control.

result.choiceRationale: R-P5 is the most closable candidate: mechanism selection is largely complete, both mechanisms survived selected physical attacks, and the remaining work is final portable/physical gates, source commit, and structured self-release — a concrete, near-term closure path with high expected frontier delta (defect-discovery or owner-mechanism-change upon graduation). G-AF3 is high-value (robustness/generalization claims not yet earned) but is an open-ended experiment start with lower closability in one budget unit. HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit that may be a no-op if the narrower surface is not justified. H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery and should be deferred. F-C2-BLOCKED is a negative control whose dominant blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) does not exist yet — defer per admission principle.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether R-P5's final portable/physical gates pass and enable a clean structured self-release (closure), versus revealing a defect that reopens mechanism selection.
result.selectionFalsifier: If R-P5's final gates expose a previously-unseen defect requiring mechanism re-selection (rather than a clean closeout), then G-AF3's open-ended robustness experiment would have been the better budget allocation.
